sources.title: AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
AMD Form 8-K: World Labs acquisition agreement

claims.text: AMD designs processors, accelerators and adaptive-computing products sold into data centers, PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Manufacturing relies on external foundries.
The Q2 2026 report uses Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded segments. Client and Gaming are combined for segment reporting, despite separate business revenue disclosures.
Core families include EPYC server CPUs, Instinct accelerators, Ryzen PC processors, Radeon graphics and adaptive SoCs/FPGAs. Software tools support deployment and programmability.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Products; Design Platforms and Services

claims.text: AMD sells through OEMs, hyperscalers, distributors and system integrators. Certain customers pay engineering fees for design and development and purchase the resulting chips.
TSMC supplies wafers for high-performance and adaptive products; GlobalFoundries supplies specified older process nodes. Product execution therefore depends on both design and outsourced capacity.
Intel competes in CPUs; NVIDIA competes in GPUs and data-center acceleration. Customer-designed processors and accelerators also constrain the addressable market.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Competition in Data Center and Client and Gaming

claims.text: Interpretation: a broad compute portfolio and software support can aid system adoption, but competitiveness requires timely launches, power efficiency and customer qualification. Portfolio breadth alone does not prove pricing power.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Competition and Research and Development

claims.text: Management expects EPYC demand, Instinct deployments and the Helios ramp to support second-half 2026 growth. These are management expectations, not a committed revenue schedule.

For Q2 2026 ended June 27, GAAP revenue was USD 11,536 million, operating income USD 1,990 million and net income USD 2,297 million. Prior-year comparisons require considering the MI308 export-control inventory charge.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations; MD&A Executive Summary

claims.text: AMD completed a senior-note offering on August 17, 2026, after the quarter-end balance sheet. In September it agreed to acquire World Labs using shares, so quarter-end debt and share counts are insufficient for a current capitalization.

evidence.locator: Item 1.01, completed offering and use of proceeds

claims.text: The earnings release names Lisa Su as chair/CEO and Jean Hu as CFO. The August 19 board change appointed Tim Ryan and made KC McClure chair of Audit and Finance.

evidence.locator: Item 5.02, Director Retirement and Director Appointment

valuation-context.unavailable: No market-price snapshot or forecast valuation is included. Update debt and potential acquisition dilution before calculating enterprise value or per-share scenarios; compare GAAP and adjusted earnings consistently.

claims.text: The Helios rollout and Instinct deployments are operational checkpoints for the second-half outlook. The packet does not assume that partnership announcements automatically convert to completed deployments or recognized revenue.

evidence.locator: CEO commentary and Recent PR Highlights

claims.text: Export controls, memory availability and third-party manufacturing constrain execution. Interpretation: delayed deployment or weak platform adoption despite product spending would challenge the growth case.

Interpretation: bull assumes successful accelerator scaling; base assumes product ramps with mixed end markets; bear assumes export restrictions and competitive displacement. Validate software readiness and customer economics before quantifying these scenarios.

World Labs is a proposed acquisition counterparty. The September filing describes share consideration with the share count determined near closing; it does not establish that the acquisition has closed.

evidence.locator: Item 3.02, Merger Agreement and share-pricing terms

claims.text: The World Labs agreement was signed September 26 and disclosed September 28, 2026. Separately, the February 4 annual-report amendment corrected transposed Client ASP and unit-growth disclosures; use the amended MD&A for historical comparisons.

gaps: Independent human review remains outstanding; this packet has received a Codex AI claim-level source review.
The FY2025 10-K/A corrects Client ASP and unit-shipment growth; no figures from the superseded narrative are carried into this packet.
SEC inventory was checked through 2026-10-18 and post-quarter 8-Ks were read; other investor announcements have not been exhaustively covered.
Current debt, acquisition dilution, valuation, customer concentration and product economics require further work.
